title: Priority-fair Admission Controller and Tiered Degradation Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have recurring incidents where cross-tenant burst traffic causes sustained CPU/GPU pressure in a single region, causing P95/P99 latency SLO violations and downstream retries. Existing shedding experiments focus on coarse rate limits and full-request rejections. We need a production-ready, priority-fair admission controller that enforces multi-dimensional admission (tenant priority, route importance, SLA tier, recent error/burn rate) and a documented set of graceful degradation modes the router can apply when admission decisions alone are insufficient.

Goals: 1) Prevent region-wide SLO burn by shedding traffic deterministically and fairly across tenants and routes. 2) Provide tiered degradation options (response trimming, model fallback, cached/placeholder responses) to preserve user-visible availability while reducing resource usage. 3) Integrate with multi-region failover so that the controller can coordinate shedding vs multi-region routing decisions. 4) Expose observability (per-tenant shed events, admission outcomes, reason codes, SLO burn impact) for post-incident analysis and automated runbook triggers.

Proposed design summary: - Priority slotting: compute a composite priority score per request = f(tenant_tier, route_priority, request_urgency_hint, recent_burn). Map scores into finite priority bands (e.g., critical, high, normal, best-effort). - Tokenized admission: maintain per-band token buckets sized by provisioned capacity and dynamic SLO headroom; admission consumes tokens. - Fairness allocator: when aggregate demand exceeds tokens, allocate remaining tokens across tenants within a band using weighted round-robin that accounts for long-term share and recent shedding history to avoid starvation. - Degradation policy engine: rather than binary accept/reject, support ordered degradation actions: 1) serve from KV prefix cache or recent response cache, 2) reduce model tier (v2 -> v1 quantized) with preserved output schema, 3) truncate/stream with early-termination token limit, 4) synthesize placeholder response with clear deprecation header, 5) reject with structured error suggesting retry/backoff. Policies are configurable per-route and per-tenant. - Circuit breaker hooks: tie to runtime error-rate and GPU OOM signals; when tripped, escalate to stricter token budgets and increase degradation aggressiveness. - Multi-region coordination: the controller exposes metrics and an API that the global router uses to decide whether to failover traffic; prefer steering overflow to healthier regions before applying destructive degradations for critical tenants.

Observability & metrics: Emit structured events for each admission decision with fields: request_id, tenant_id, priority_band, action_taken, tokens_consumed, reason_code. Key metrics: per-tenant shed_rate, per-route shed_rate, admission_success_ratio, p50/p95/p99 latencies pre/post-shedding, SLO burn rate, fairness_violation_count. Build dashboards and an automated alert when cluster-level shed_rate > X% and mapped to high SLO burn.

Acceptance criteria: - Admission controller deployed to staging, handling real traffic replay with canary at 10% in us-west-2 without increased error budget burn. - Degradation actions implemented for cached fallback and model-tier fallback with opt-in per-route config. - Exposed telemetry validated in Grafana dashboards and feeding to incident runbooks. - Automated e2e test harness that simulates tenant bursts and verifies fair token allocation and that critical-band requests maintain >95% success under load.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement admission-control server and local sim harness (Sprint 1). 2) Add degradation policy plugins and integrate with model selection (Sprint 2). 3) Deploy to staging, run synthetic storm tests and replay production traces (Sprint 3). 4) Canary deploy to us-west-2 at 10% traffic; monitor for 72 hours; expand to other regions in phased manner.

Runbook snippets: - If cluster shed_rate spikes >20%: enable emergency throttling for non-critical bands, increase model-tier fallback ratio by 2x, and notify SRE. - If fairness_violation_count > 50 over 10m: temporarily increase per-tenant minimum allocation and investigate offending tenant.

Security & compliance notes: The admission controller consults tenant metadata (tier, SLA) stored in our config service; ensure reads are audited. Telemetry events should avoid including PII; use hashed tenant IDs in public dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller accepts or degrades requests per configured policy with >=95% success for critical-band under synthetic bursts
Two degradation modes implemented (cache fallback + model-tier fallback) and toggled via per-route config
Structured admission events emitted and ingested into observability pipeline within 5s latency
Canary at 10% in us-west-2 runs 72 hours with <10% additional SLO burn compared to baseline
